reason: The current graph-and-history model reaches macro validation HR@10 of 0.6112, but training propagation includes the very edges being supervised; removing those edges tests a plausible training–inference mismatch without attributing Electronics’ 0.400 score to an established cause. Modify model_design for minibatch-specific propagation and training_evaluation for integration, diagnostics, and full-graph checkpoint/predictor consistency. Historical objective replacements failed while successful experiments isolated targeted changes, supporting retention of the current architecture and loss.

plan.model_design: In GraphRecommender.forward(self, users, positives, negatives, histories=None), use a temporary graph during training that excludes every distinct minibatch (users, positives) edge in both directions, while preserving existing variable names and public function signatures. Recover the unique unweighted user–item topology from adjacency’s sparse indices, cache only nonpersistent topology metadata, encode supervised pairs as users * (itemnum + 1) + positives, deduplicate these keys, and remove matching edges regardless of repeated target occurrences or earlier occurrences in supplied histories. Recompute node degrees from the remaining topology and symmetric weights as d(u)^(-1/2) * d(i)^(-1/2), using clamped degrees for isolated nodes, then propagate all layers over this same temporary graph through a private helper; do not merely remove entries from the previously normalized adjacency. Keep propagate() and prepare_inference() operating on the complete training-only adjacency, leave the persistent adjacency buffer untouched, and never cache minibatch-specific embeddings for inference. Preserve history attention, supplied histories, embeddings, graph depth, score computation, current sampled-softmax loss, regularization, optimizer, negative sampling, and every model hyperparameter, isolating edge masking rather than importing historical Transformer, recency-weighting, or objective changes.
plan.training_evaluation: Retain train_category(name, device), build_graph(train, user_ids, itemnum), evaluate, check_history_fusion, write_predictor(), and generated predict signatures, integrating masking through the existing training forward call and clearing _cached before training updates. Extend the existing charged diagnostics with deterministic checks that duplicate supervised pairs remove exactly one undirected edge, both directions disappear, retained weights match recomputed degrees, isolated nodes remain finite, and the persistent full adjacency is unchanged; keep diagnostics inside the existing RNG-forking mechanism. Preserve complete-graph validation and checkpoint serialization, and update write_predictor() explicitly to reconstruct the same architecture, strictly load the full training adjacency, and call prepare_inference() without applying minibatch masks, with prediction parity checked after reloading the same model. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training/evaluation seeds 42, supplied splits, all four categories and routing, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, EPOCHS default 200, existing batch size, steps, learning rate, category time cap, patience, validation schedule, HR@10/NDCG checkpoint selection, and pinned validation using 200 users/category with 99 unique negatives unchanged. Train each category from scratch and load exactly one selected checkpoint per category, prohibit ensembles, averaging, separately fitted scorers, other-trial checkpoint reuse, extra data, hidden-test access, and evaluator changes, and assess the hypothesized 0.005–0.015 macro HR@10 gain over 0.6112 through measured host validation results and category regressions.
